source_predecessors.quote:
Die breiten GDT427-Klassen verschlucken die Wortbedeutungen nicht. Wir finden
**104 exakte Austauschrahmen**: Eine Handlung wird durch eine andere ersetzt,
während jede übrige Komponente und ihre Position gleich bleibt.

Beispiele der Form sind `@ACTION+AIIN`, `@ACTION+AL`, `@ACTION+EE+DY` oder
`CH+@ACTION+E+Y`. Das sieht genau nach einer kleinen produktiven
Kürzelgrammatik aus: Der Rahmen bleibt, das Handlungskürzel wechselt, und damit
wechselt der Arbeitsgang.

Die gleiche Methode wie bei den neun Handlungen findet **256 exakte
Austauschrahmen** für die zehn übrigen Kerne. Argumente, Relationen und
Reihenfolgezeichen sitzen also in produktiven Slots. Trotzdem sind ihre kurzen
Bedeutungen nicht beliebig austauschbar.

reviews.title: A contrast marker selects between explicitly opposed alternatives
reviews.finding: The mechanism is coherent only after opposition is typed. Its prediction does not follow as written: alternatives may be scalar or pragmatically contrasted while both remain jointly true (e.g. “warm and fragrant”), and a generic connector can occur between alternatives. The falsifier “alternatives are not mutually exclusive” therefore rejects one unannounced exclusivity variant, not contrast marking generally.
reviews.counterexample: “Tea or coffee, preferably tea” is contrastive/alternative but not a binary factually exclusive pair; “wood and charcoal differ in color” contrasts two jointly asserted items.
reviews.repair: Predeclare exclusive, scalar, or corrective opposition as separate models; independently code alternative relation and polarity; use matched generic connectors. Treat absence of the selected opposition pattern as a model-specific failure, while non-exclusivity alone is not a falsifier.

reviews.title: A coordination marker scopes over a multi-item list
reviews.finding: Shared-predicate/list structure is not entailed by coordination. Coordination can join items with separate predicates (“wood burns and charcoal smolders”), while an item noun can appear in a shared-predicate list (“wood and charcoal burn”). Thus “fewer independent predicate assignments” does not distinguish coordination from the item-noun rival without an independently frozen parse.
reviews.counterexample: “Add salt and stir” coordinates two clauses/operations with no one shared predicate; “wood and charcoal burn” has a shared predicate although both nouns remain independently typed items.
reviews.repair: Define the unit as a frozen syntactic coordination parse with independently typed conjuncts, compare shared and separate predicates, and make the rival predict a concrete alternative parse. Segmentation ambiguity is a capacity stop until resolved, not by itself evidence against coordination.

overall: Both designs are useful shortlist questions but neither current falsifier follows from its broad mechanism. GDT428/GDT429 establish exchange-frame observations and working contrasts, not independent opposition, list-scope, or English meaning bindings. No readiness or semantic confirmation follows.
